pp:ce:2003:q1.question: Given Matrix $$[A]=\begin{bmatrix} 4 & 2 & 1 &3 \\ 6&3 &4 & 7\\ 2 &1 & 0& 1 \end{bmatrix}$$, the rank of the matrix is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Linear Algebra
detailed_solution.markdown:
Consider first $3\times 3$ minors, since maximum possible rank is 3

$$\begin{aligned} \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 2 &1 \\ 6 & 3 & 4\\ 2 & 1 & 0 \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\  \begin{vmatrix} 2 & 1 &3 \\ 3 & 4& 7\\ 1 & 0& 1 \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\  \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 1 & 3\\ 6 & 4 & 7\\ 2 & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}&=0\\ \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 2 &3 \\ 6 & 3 & 7\\ 2 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}&=0 \end{aligned}$$

Since all $3\times 3$

minors are zero, now try $2\times 2$ minors.

$$\begin{aligned} \begin{vmatrix} 4 &2 \\ 6 & 3 \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\  \begin{vmatrix} 2 &1 \\ 3 & 4 \end{vmatrix}&=8-3=5\neq 0 \\ \therefore\;\; \text{rank }&=2 \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2003:q2.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ce:2003:q2.question:
A box contains 10 screws, 3 of which are defective. Two screws are drawn at
random with replacement. The probability that none of the two screws is defective
will be

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Probability and Statistics
detailed_solution.markdown:
Total number of screws = 10

Number of defective screws = 3

Number of non-defective screws = $10 - 3 = 7$

Probability of selecting a non-defective screw in one draw:

$P(\text{non-defective}) = \frac{7}{10}$

Since the screws are drawn with replacement, the two events are independent. So, the probability that both screws drawn are non-defective is:

$P(\text{both non-defective}) = \left(\frac{7}{10}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{100} = 0.49$

Hence, the required probability is 49%.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2003:q3.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ce:2003:q3.question:
If P, Q and R are three points having coordinates (3,-2,-1), (1,3,4), (2,1,-2)
in XYZ space, then the distance from point P to plane OQR (O being the origin
of the coordinate system) is given by

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Calculus
detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, $$\begin{aligned} P\left ( 3,-2,-1 \right ) &\\   Q\left ( 1,3,4 \right ) &\\   R\left ( 2,1,-2 \right ) &\\   O\left ( 0,0,0 \right )&\\ \text{Equation of plane OQR is,}&\\ \begin{vmatrix} x-x_{1} & y-y_{1} & z-z_{1}\\ x_{2}-x_{1} & y_{2}-y_{1} & z_{2}-z_{1}\\ x_{3}-x_{1} & y_{3}-y_{1} & z_{3}-z_{1} \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\ \begin{vmatrix} x-0 & y-0 & z-0\\ 1 & 3 & 4\\ 2 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}&=0\\ \text{i.e., }2x-2y+z&=0 \end{aligned}$$

Now $\perp$

distance of $\left ( x_{1},\: y_{1},\: z_{1} \right )$ from $ax + by + cz + d=0$ is given by,

$\left | \frac{ax_{1}+by_{1}+cz_{1}+d}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}}} \right |$

Therefore, $\perp$

distance of (3, -2, 1) from plane $2x-2y+z=0$ is given by,

$\left | \frac{2\times 3-2\times \left ( -2 \right )+\left ( -1 \right )}{\sqrt{2^{2}+\left ( -2 \right )^{2}+1^{2}}} \right |=3$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2003:q12.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 12

detailed_solution.concept: Structural Analysis - Matrix Method of Structural Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown:
The beam will deflect in symmetric mode when a constant moment M is applied at both ends. Slope at either ends will be given as $\frac{M L}{2 E I}$. We know that stiffness is the moment required to produce unit slope.

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \theta&=\frac{M L}{2 E I} \\ \Rightarrow \quad M&=\frac{2 E I}{L} \theta &[\because \theta=1]\\ \Rightarrow \quad M&=\frac{2 E I}{L}=K \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Seepage Analysis

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Stability Analysis of Slopes

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Given }\phi^{\prime}&=35^{\circ}: \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}=20 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ F&=1.5 ; \beta=? ; \gamma=\gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}-\gamma_{\mathrm{w}} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2003:q18.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 18
pp:ce:2003:q18.question: For a two-dimensional irrotational flow, the velocity potential defined as $\phi =ln(x^{2}+y^{2})$ . Which of the following is a possible stream function, $\psi$ for this flow ?

$$\begin{aligned}

\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial y} &=\frac{\partial}{\partial x} \log _{e}\left(x^{2}+y^{2}\right)\\

\end{aligned}$$

Integrating both sides, we get

$$\begin{aligned}

\psi&=\int \frac{2 x}{x^{2}+y^{2}} d y+C\\

\Rightarrow \quad \Psi&=2 x\times \frac{1}{x} \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+C \\

\Rightarrow \quad \Psi&=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)+C

\end{aligned}$$

However, it may be noted that 'C' is a function of x

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{Q_{m}}{Q_{p}}&=\frac{\left(L_{m}\right)^{3} / T_{m}}{\left(L_{p}\right)^{3} / T_{D}} \qquad\left[\because \frac{L_{m}}{T_{m}}=V_{m}\right]\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{Q_{m}}{Q_{p}}&=\frac{V_{m}\left(L_{m}\right)^{2}}{V_{p}\left(L_{p}\right)^{2}} \quad\left[\because v_{1}=\sqrt{L}\right] \\ \Rightarrow \frac{Q_{m}}{Q_{p}}&=\left(\frac{L_{m}}{L_{D}}\right)^{5 / 2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad Q_{m}&=Q_{p} \times\left(\frac{L_{m}}{L_{p}}\right)^{5 / 2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad Q_{m}&=10.000 \times\left(\frac{1}{100}\right)^{5 / 2} \\ &=0.1 \mathrm{m}^{3}/s \end{aligned}$$

By Theim's formula, the discharge rate for an

pp:ce:2003:q22.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 22
pp:ce:2003:q22.question:
The vertical hydraulic conductivity of the top soil at certain stage is 0.2 cm/hr. A storm of intensity 0.5 cm/hr occurs over the soil for an indefinite period.
Assuming the surfaces drainage to be adequate, the infiltration rate after the
storm has lasted for a very long time, shall be

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Infiltration, Runoff and Hydrographs
detailed_solution.markdown:
Permeability = Hydraulic conductivity $\left ( \frac{\mu }{\rho g} \right )$

A storm of i=0.5 cm/hr occurs over the soil for an indefinite period.

What is the meaning of "indefinite period"?

In order to achieve steady state condition, continuous application of water is necessary so that the water level is maintained constant.

'Surface drainage adequate' means at steady state condition some water flows as surface runoff.

'Storm has lasted for a very long time' means the hydraulic conductivity approaches saturated hydraulic conductivity (so that Darcy's law can be obeyed) and at steady state condition infiltration rate is also constant.

The constant infiltration rate which is achieved after very long time, shall be more than 0.2 cm/hr (as hydraulic conductivity has increased) but should be less than storm intensity 0.5 cm/hr due to adequate drainage.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Partial Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
$$\begin{aligned}  L\left [ f\left ( t \right ) \right ]&=\int_{0}^{\infty }e^{-st}f\left ( t \right )dt \\ \therefore \;\; L\left [ \sin \left ( at \right ) \right ]&=\int_{0}^{\infty }e^{-st}\sin \left ( at \right )dt \\ &=    \frac{a}{s^{2}+a^{2}} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2003:q32.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 32
pp:ce:2003:q32.question:
The Fourier series expansion of a symmetric and even function, f(x) where $$\begin{matrix} f(x) &=1+(2x/\pi), & \; -\pi \lt x \lt 0 \\ &=1-(2x/\pi), & \; 0 \lt x \lt \pi \end{matrix}$$
will be

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Mathematics - Partial Differential Equation
detailed_solution.markdown:
Since given function is symmetric and even, its Fourier series contain only cosine terms.

$$\begin{aligned} a_{0}&=\frac{2}{c}\int_{0}^{c}f\left ( x \right )dx\\ \text{and }  a_{n}&=\frac{2}{c}\int_{0}^{c}f\left ( x \right )\cos \frac{n\pi x}{c}dx\\ &\text{Using above result and using,}\\  f\left ( x \right )&=1-\frac{2x}{\pi } \text{ we get}\\  a_{0}&=\frac{2}{\pi }\int_{0}^{\pi }\left ( 1-\frac{2x}{\pi } \right )dx \\ &=\frac{2}{\pi }\left ( x-\frac{x^{2}}{\pi } \right )_{0}^{\pi }=0 \\ \text{and  } a_{n}&=\frac{2}{\pi }\int_{0}^{\pi }\left ( 1-\frac{2x}{\pi } \right )\cos nx\: dx \\   &=\frac{2}{\pi }\left [ \left ( 1-\frac{2x}{\pi } \right )\frac{\sin nx}{n}-\left ( -\frac{2}{\pi } \right )\left ( -\frac{\cos nx}{n^{2}} \right ) \right ]_{0}^{\pi } \\   &=\frac{2}{\pi }\left [ -\frac{2\cos n\pi }{\pi n^{2}}+\frac{2}{\pi n^{2}} \right ] \\   &=\frac{4}{n^{2}\pi ^{2}}\left [ 1-\cos n\pi \right ]\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2003:q33.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 33
pp:ce:2003:q33.question:
A long structural column (length= L) with both ends hinged is acted upon by an axial compressive load, P. The differential equation governing the bending of column is given by :
$EI\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=-Py$
Where y is the structural lateral deflection and EI is the flexural rigidity. The first critical load on column responsible for its buckling is given by

primary.subtopicLabel: Theory of Columns and Shear Centre

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Theory of Columns and Shear Centre
detailed_solution.markdown:
Differential equation governing the bending of column

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{E I d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}&=-P y\\ \Rightarrow \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}+\frac{P}{E I} y&=0 \end{aligned}$$

Solution of differential equation

$$\begin{aligned} y&=A\cos\left(x \sqrt{\frac{P}{E I}}\right)+B \sin \left(x \sqrt{\frac{P}{E I}}\right)\\ \text{when }x=0 . y&=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0&=B \sin \left(L \sqrt{\frac{P}{E I}}\right) \\ \therefore \quad L \sqrt{\frac{P}{E I}}&=x\text{ (First value)}\\ \Rightarrow P&=\frac{\pi^{2} E I}{L^{2}} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2003:q34.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 34
pp:ce:2003:q34.question: In a redundant joint model, three bar members are pin connected at Q as shown in the figure. Under some load placed at Q, the elongation of the members MQ and OQ are found to be 48 mm and 35 mm respectively. Then the horizontal displacement 'u' and the vertical displacement 'v' of the node Q, in mm, will be respectively,

detailed_solution.concept: Structural Analysis - Trusses
detailed_solution.markdown: $\text { Let } \angle M Q N=\theta_{1} \text { and } \angle O Q N=\theta_{2}$ $$\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \tan \theta_{1}&=\frac{M N}{N Q}=\frac{400}{500}=0.8 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \sin \theta_{1}&=0.625 \\ \text{ and }\cos \theta_{1}&=0.781 \\ \text{and }\tan \theta_{2}&=\frac{N O}{N Q}=\frac{500}{500}=1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \sin \theta_{2}&=0.707 \\ \text{ and }\cos \theta_{2}&=0.707 \\ \end{aligned}$$ Elongation of member MQ in terms of u and v will be, $$\begin{aligned} u \sin \theta_{1}+v \cos \theta_{1}&=48 \\ \text{or, }0.625 u+0.781 v&=48 \quad &\ldots(i) \end{aligned}$$ Elongation of member OQ in terms of u and v will be, $$\begin{aligned} \text{or, }-u \sin \theta_{2}+v \cos \theta_{2}&=35 \\ -0.707 u+0.707 v&=35 \quad \ldots(ii) \end{aligned}$$ Solving (i) and (ii) we get, $u=6.64 \mathrm{mm}\text{ and }v=56.14 \mathrm{mm}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2003:q35.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:ce:2003:q35.question: Top ring beam of an Intze tank carries a hoop tension of 120 kN. The beam cross-section is 250 mm wide and 400 mm deep and it is reinforced with 4 bars of 20 mm diameter of Fe-415 grade. Molular ratio of the concrete is 10. The tensile stress in N/$mm^{2}$ in the concrete is

detailed_solution.concept: RCC Structures - Footing, Columns, Beams and Slabs
detailed_solution.markdown:
The tensile stress in the concrete is given by,

$$\begin{aligned} \sigma_{t} &=\frac{\text { Hoop tension }}{(b \times d)+(m-1) A_{s t}} \\ &=\frac{120 \times 10^{3}}{(250 \times 400)+(10-1) \times 4 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times(20)^{2}} \\ &=1.07 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2003:q36.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 36
pp:ce:2003:q36.question: A "H" shaped frame of uniform flexural rigidity EI is loaded as shown in the figure. The relative outward displacement between points K and O is

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Deflection of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown:
The bending moment in the member

$\mathrm{JN}=\mathrm{R} \times \mathrm{h}(sagging)$

$\therefore\text{ Slope at J or N}=\frac{R h \times L}{2 E I}$

Thus, outward displacement between points

$K\text{ and }O=\frac{R h L}{2 E I} \times h+\frac{R h L}{2 E I} \times h=\frac{R h^{2} L}{E I}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2003:q37.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 37
pp:ce:2003:q37.question: A simply supported beam of uniform rectangular cross-section of width b and depth h is subjected to linear temperature gradient 0$^{\circ}$ at the top and T$^{\circ}$ at the bottom, as shown in the figure. The coefficient of linear expansion of the beam material is $\alpha$. The resulting vertical deflection at the mid-span of the beam is

detailed_solution.concept: Solid Mechanics - Deflection of Beams
detailed_solution.markdown:
The average change in temperature $=\frac{T}{2}$

The compression in the top most fibre

$=\alpha \times L \times \frac{T}{2}$

Similarly, the elongation in bottom most fibre

$$\begin{aligned} &=\alpha \times L \times \frac{T}{2}\\ \therefore\text{ Strain, }\varepsilon_{0}&=\frac{L \alpha T}{L \times 2}=\frac{\alpha T}{2} \\ \end{aligned}$$

Therefore deflection at midpoint is downward. Now, from the equation of pure bending, we have

$\frac{M}{I}=\frac{E}{R}=\frac{f}{y}$

$\Rightarrow$ Curvature,

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{R} &=\frac{f}{E y}=\frac{\text { Strain }}{y}\left[\because y=\frac{h}{2}\right] \\ &=\frac{2 \varepsilon_{0}}{h}=\frac{\alpha T}{h} \end{aligned}$$

Also, from the property of circle, we have

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Deflection, }\delta&=\frac{L^{2}}{8 R}=\frac{L^{2}}{8} \times \frac{\alpha T}{h} \\ &=\frac{\alpha T L^{2}}{8 h} \text { downward } \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ce:2003:q38.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 38
pp:ce:2003:q38.question: A truss, as shown in the figure, is carrying 180 kN load at node $L_2$. The force in the diagonal member $M_2U_4$ will be

detailed_solution.concept: Structural Analysis - Trusses
detailed_solution.markdown: Let reactions at $L_{0}$ and $L_{6}$ be $R_{L_{0}}$ and $R_{L_{6}}$ respectively. $\therefore R_{L_{0}}+R_{L_{6}}=180 \qquad\ldots(i)$ Taking moments about $L_{0}$ , we get, $R_{L_{6}} \times 24-180 \times 8=0$ $\Rightarrow \quad R_{L_{6}}=60 \mathrm{kN}$ $\therefore$From (i), we get, $R_{L_{0}}=120 \mathrm{kN}$ Assuming a section passing through members $U_{3} U_{4}, M_{2} L_{3}$ and $L_{3} L_{4}$ and considering left portion Taking moments about $L_{3}=0$ $\Rightarrow 120 \times 12-180 \times 4+F_{U_{3}} u_{4} \times 3=0$ $\Rightarrow F_{U_{3} U_{4}}=-240 \mathrm{kN}=240 \mathrm{kN}$ (compression) Now assuming a section passing through members $U_{3} U_{4}, M_{2} U_{4}, M_{2} L_{4}$ and $L_{3} L_{4}$ and considering right portion. $\cos \theta=\frac{3}{5} ; \sin \theta=\frac{4}{5}$ Taking moments about $L_{4}=0$ $$\begin{array}{l} F_{U_{3} U_{4}} \times 3-\left(F_{M_{2} U_{4}} \sin \theta\right) \times 3-60 \times 8=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 240 \times 3-480=F_{M_{2} U_{4}} \times 3 \times \frac{4}{5} \\ \Rightarrow \quad F_{M_{2} U_{4}}=100 \mathrm{kN} (tension) \end{array}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2003:q39.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 39
pp:ce:2003:q39.question: A steel portal frame has dimensions, plastic moment capacities and applied loads as shown in the figure. The vertical load is always twice of the horizontal load. The collapse load P required for the development of a beam mechanism is

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Plastic Analysis
detailed_solution.markdown: The possible locations of the plastic hinges are at A, B, C, D and E. Number of plastic hinges, $N= 5$ Degree of redundancy, $r=6-3=3$ Number of possible independent mechanisms, $n=N-r=5-3=2$ Thus the two independent mechanisms are 1. Beam mechanisms 2. Sway mechanism Beam mechanism: The ends B and D of the frame ABCD are fixed joints. Therefore, the beam BD acts as a fixed end beam. $$\begin{aligned} &\text{External work done}\\ &=\text{load} \times \text{deflection} \\ &=2P\times \Delta =2P\times L\times \theta \\ &=2PL\theta\\ & \text{Internal work done} \\ &=\text{moment} \times \text{rotation} \\ &=M_{P}\theta +2M_{P}\left ( \theta +\theta \right )+M_{P}\theta \\ &=6M_{P}\theta \end{aligned}$$ By principal of virtual work, External work done = Internal work done $\; \; 2PL\theta =6M_{P}\theta$ $\Rightarrow \; P=\, \frac{3M_{P}}{L}$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2003:q40.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 40
pp:ce:2003:q40.question:
The state of two dimensional stresses acting on a concrete lamina consists of a
direct tensile stress, $\sigma _{x}$=1.5 $N/mm^{2}$, and shear stress, $\tau$ = 1.20 $N/mm^{2}$, which cause cracking of concrete. Then the tensile strength of the concrete in $N/mm^{2}$ is

Maximum principal stress

&=\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{x}}}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{\sigma_{\mathrm{x}}}{2}\right)^{2}+\tau^{2}} \\

&=2.17 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2}

\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2003:q45.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 45
pp:ce:2003:q45.question: Compaction of an embankment is carried out in 500 mm thick layers. The rammer used for compaction has a foot area of 0.05 $m^{2}$ and the energy imparted in every drop of rammer is 400 Nm. Assuming 50% more energy in each pass over the compacted area due to overlap, the number of passes required to develop compactive energy equivalent of Indian Standard light compaction for each layer would be

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Compaction of Soil
detailed_solution.markdown:
As per Indian Standard light compaction test, a

hammer of 2.6 kg is allowed to fall from a height of

310 mm and 3 layers are tamped 25 times in a

mould of volume 1000 cc .

$\therefore$ Energy imparted

$$\begin{array}{l} =2.6 \times 25 \times 3 \times 9.81 \\ \times \frac{310}{1000}=593.01 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m} \end{array}$$

For embankment compaction, the volume of soil covered by rammer

$$\begin{aligned} &=0.05 \times 10^{4} \times \frac{500}{10} \\ &=25000 \mathrm{cc} \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore$ Energy imparted in every drop of hammer

$$\begin{aligned} &=\left(1+\frac{50}{100}\right) \times 400\\ &=600 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

If 'n' number of passes are required to develop equivalent energy to Indian Standard light compaction test, then

$n \times \frac{600}{25000}=\frac{593.01}{1000}$

$\Rightarrow \quad n=24.71 \simeq 25\text{( approx.)}$

However, If the data of Standard Proctor Test are taken i.e. weight of hammer =2.495 kg; Volume of mould =944cc, then the value of 'n' will be close to 26.

Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ce:2003:q46.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 46
pp:ce:2003:q46.question:
A braced cut, 5 m wide and 7.5 m deep is proposed in a cohesionless soil deposit
having effective cohesion c'=0 and effective friction angle, ${\phi}' =36^{\circ}$. The first row of struts is to be installed at a depth of 0.5 m below ground surface and spacing between the struts should be 1.5 m. If the horizontal spacing of struts is 3 m and unit weight of the deposit is 20 $kN/m^{3}$, the maximum strut load will be

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Retaining Wall-Earth Pressure Theories
detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} K_{a} &=\frac{1-\sin \phi^{\prime}}{1+\sin \phi^{\prime}} \\ &=\frac{1-\sin 36^{\circ}}{1+\sin 36^{\circ}}=0.2596 \end{aligned}$$ $\therefore$ Uniform pressure on side of cut $$\begin{aligned} &=0.65 \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}} \gamma \mathrm{H} \\ &=0.65 \times 0.2596 \times 20 \times 7.5 \\ &=25.31 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Area covered by strut $$\begin{aligned} 1 &=3 \times(0.5+0.75) \\ &=3.75 \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Area covered by strut 2 and downward struts $=3 \times(0.75+0.75)=4.5 \mathrm{m}^{2}$ $\therefore$ Maximum force will be carried by strut 2 and downward struts $$\begin{aligned} &=25.31 \times 4.5=113.89 \mathrm{kN} \\ &\simeq 113.90 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

$=h \gamma_{w}=2 \times 10=20 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$

Consolidation settlement of the clay layer

detailed_solution.markdown: Assume equivalent raft at a distance of $\frac{L}{3}=\frac{5}{3}$ from the bottom of the pipe and load dispersion at $2 \mathrm{H}: 1 \mathrm{V}$ Compressible layer thickness $=7-5+\frac{5}{3}=3.667 \mathrm{m}$ Average stress at the center of layer, $$\begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{0}=& \gamma_{\text {sub }} \times 5.17 \\ &=(20-10) \times 5.17 \\ &=51.7 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$ Increased width of equivalent raft at depth $=1.2+\frac{\left(\frac{5}{3}+2\right)}{2}=3.03 \mathrm{m}$ Pressure increase due to load on pile, $$\begin{aligned} \Delta \sigma &=\frac{500}{3.03^{2}}=54.34 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \Delta H &=\frac{C_{c} H_{0}}{1+e_{0}} \log \left(\frac{\bar{\sigma}_{0}+\Delta \sigma}{\bar{\sigma}_{0}}\right) \\ &=\frac{0.027 \times \frac{11}{3}}{1+1.05} \log \left(\frac{51.7+54.34}{51.7}\right) \\ &=15.07 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **D**.

pp:ce:2003:q52.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 52
pp:ce:2003:q52.question: A horizontal jet strikes a frictionless vertical plate (the plan view is shown in the figure). It is then divided into two parts, as shown in the figure. If the impact loss is neglected, what is the value of $\theta$?

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Impact of Jets and Turbines
detailed_solution.markdown:
From continuity equation, we get,

$$\begin{aligned} & & Q_{0}=Q_{1}+Q_{2} \\ \Rightarrow & & Q_{0}=0.25 Q_{0}+Q_{2} \\ \Rightarrow & & Q_{2}=0.75 Q_{0} \end{aligned}$$

since, the impact losses are neglected, the velocity will remain unchanged in the direction of $Q_{1}$ and $Q_{2}$

$\text{i.e.},\quad V_{0}=V_{1}=V_{2}$

Applying impulse momentum equation, we get,

$$\begin{aligned} \rho Q_{0} V_{0} \sin \theta&=\rho Q_{2} V_{2}-\rho Q_{1} V_{1} \\ \Rightarrow \quad Q_{0} \sin \theta&=0.75 Q_{0}-0.25 Q_{0} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \sin \theta&=1 / 2 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \theta&=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

pp:ce:2003:q53.question: A hydraulic jump takes place in a triangular channel of vertex angle 90$^{\circ}$, as shown in figure. The discharge is 1 $m^{3}/s$ and the pre-jump depth is 0.5 m. What will be the post-jump depth ? (Take g = 981 $m/s^{2}$)

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
Specific force will remain constant on both sides of hydraulic jump.

$$\begin{aligned} \therefore \frac{Q^{2}}{g A_{1}}+A_{1} \bar{Z}_{1} &=\frac{Q^{2}}{g A_{2}}+A_{2} \bar{Z}_{2} \\ A_{1} &=y_{1}^{2} ; A_{2}=y_{2}^{2} \\ \bar{Z}_{1} &=\left(\frac{y_{1}}{3}\right) ; \quad \bar{Z}_{2}=\left(\frac{y_{2}}{3}\right) \\ \text{Given}\quad Q &=1 \mathrm{m}^{3 / \mathrm{s}} ; y_{1}=0.5 \mathrm{m}\\ \therefore \frac{(1)^{2}}{9.81 \times(0.5)^{2}}&+(0.5)^{2} \times\left(\frac{0.5}{3}\right) \\ &=\frac{(1)^{2}}{9.81 \times y_{2}^{2}}+\left(y_{2}\right)^{2} \times\left(\frac{y_{2}}{3}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.4494&=\frac{0.1019}{y_{2}^{2}}+\frac{y_{2}^{3}}{3} \\ \end{aligned}$$

By hit and trial, we get $y_{2}=1.02 \mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

pp:ce:2003:q54.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 54
pp:ce:2003:q54.question: Two pipelines, one carrying oil (mass density 900 kg/$m^{3}$) and the other water, are connected to a manometer as shown in figure. By what amount the pressure in the water pipe should be increased so that the mercury levels in both the limbs of the manometer become equal ? (mass density of mercury= 13550 kg/$m^{3}$ and g = 9.81 m/$s^{2}$)

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Fluid Properties and Manometry
detailed_solution.markdown: Initially the pressure difference between water and oil can be given as $$\begin{aligned} p_{w}+(1000 &\times 9.81 \times 1.5)+(13550 \times 9.81 \times 20 \\ \left.\times 10^{-2}\right)-(900 &\times 9.81 \times 3)=p_{0}\\ \Rightarrow \; p_{w t}+14715+26585.1-26487=p_{0} \\ \Rightarrow \quad p_{0}-p_{w}&=14813.1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad P_{0}-P_{w}&=14.8 \mathrm{kPa} &\ldots(i) \end{aligned}$$ To make the same level of mercury in both the limbs, the level of mercury should be decreased by 10 cm in right limb and increased by 10cm in lett limb $$\begin{aligned} P_{w t}+(1000 \times 9.81 &\times 1.6)-(900 \times 9.81 \times 2.9)=p_{0}\\ \Rightarrow \quad P_{0}-p_{w t}&=-9.9 \mathrm{kPa} &\ldots(ii)\\ \end{aligned}$$ Subtracting (ii) from (i) we get $$\begin{array}{l} P_{W}-P_{N}=14.8+99 \\ P_{\mathrm{w} t}-P_{\mathrm{w}}=24.7 \mathrm{kPa} \text { (increase) } \end{array}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **A**.

pp:ce:2003:q55.title: GATE CE 2003 | Set 1 | Question: 55
pp:ce:2003:q55.question: A solid sphere (diameter 6 mm) is rising through oil (mass density 900 $kg/m^{3}$, dynamic viscosity 0.7 kg/ms) at a constant velocity of 1 cm/s. What is the specific weight of the material form which the sphere is made ? (Take g = 9.81 $m/s^{2}$)

primary.subtopicLabel: Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Boundary Layer Theory, Drag and Lift
detailed_solution.markdown: The solid sphere will be acted upon by three forces viz. drag force $\left(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{D}}\right)$, force of buoyancy $\left(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}\right)$ and self weight of sphere (W) $$\begin{array}{l} W=\rho_{s} V g \\ F_{B}=\rho_{0} V g \\ F_{D}=C_{D} A \frac{\rho_{0} V^{2}}{2} \end{array}$$ Reynolds Number, $$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Re} &=\frac{\rho_{0} \mathrm{VD}}{\mu} \\ &=\frac{900 \times 1 \times 10^{-2} \times 6 \times 10^{-3}}{0.7} \\ &=0.07714 \lt 0.2(\mathrm{ok}) \\\; \therefore \quad \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{D}} &=\frac{24}{\mathrm{Re}}=\frac{24}{0.07714}=311.12 \end{aligned}$$ Now, from the free body diagram, we have $W+F_{D}=F_{B}$ $$\begin{aligned} \quad W&=F_{B}-F_{D} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \rho_{s} V g&=\rho_{0} V g-C_{D} A \frac{\rho_{0} V^{2}}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad w_{\mathrm{s}} V&=\rho_{0} V g-C_{D} \frac{A \rho_{0} V^{2}}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad w_{\mathrm{s}}&=\rho_{0} g-\frac{C_{\mathrm{D}} A \rho_{0} v^{2}}{2 V} \\ \Rightarrow \quad w_{\mathrm{s}}&=900 \times 9.81 \\ & -\frac{\left[\begin{array}{l}6 \times 311.12 \times \pi \times\left(6 \times 10^{-3}\right)^{2} \\ \times 900 \times\left(1 \times 10^{-2}\right)^{2}\end{array}\right]}{4 \times \pi \times\left(6 \times 10^{-3}\right)^{3}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad w_{\mathrm{s}}&=5328.9 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^{3}=5.3 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$ Therefore, the correct answer is **B**.

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Water Treatment
detailed_solution.markdown:
Velocity of sand particles,

$$\begin{aligned} {V}'_{s} &=\frac{g}{18}\left ( S_{s}-1 \right )\frac{d^{2}}{\nu } \\ &=\frac{9.81}{18}\times \left ( 2.65-1 \right )\times \frac{\left ( 0.001\times 10^{-3} \right )^{2}}{\left ( 10^{-3}/1000 \right )} \\ &=\frac{9.81}{18}\times 1.65\times 10^{-4} \\ {V}'_{s} &=8.9925\times 10^{-5}\; \text{m/sec} \end{aligned}$$

$\text{settling time}$

$$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{\text{Volume of tank}}{\text{Water flow rate}} \\ &=\frac{900\times 3}{8000}days=\frac{2700}{8000}\times 24=8.1\; hrs \end{aligned}$$

$\text{Settling velocity,}$

$$\begin{aligned} V_{s} &=\frac{\text{Depth of tank}}{\text{Settling time}}=\frac{3}{8.1\times 3600} \\ &=1.0288\times 10^{-4}\; \text{m/s} \end{aligned}$$

$\therefore \; \;\text{ Removal efficiency}=\frac{{V}'_{s}}{V_{s}}\times 100$

$$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{8.9925\times 10^{-5}}{1.0288\times 10^{-4}}\times 100 \\ &=8.41\%\simeq 87.5\% \end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

A water treatment plant treating 10 MLD of water requires 20 mg/L of filter Alum, $AI_2(SO_4)_3.18H_2O$. The water has 6 mg/L of alkalinity as $CaCO_3$ (Al = 26.97, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1, Ca = 40 and C = 12).

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Quality Characteristics of Water

$$\left ( i \right )\; \; \begin{matrix} Al_{2}\left ( SO_{4} \right )_{3}.\: 18H_{2}O+3Ca\left ( HCO_{3} \right )_{2}\\ 666\; gm\; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \left ( 3\times 162 \right )gm \end{matrix}$$

$$\left ( ii \right )\begin{matrix} CaCO_{3}+H_{2}O+CO_{2}\rightarrow Ca\left ( HCO_{3} \right )_{2}\\ 100\: gm\; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; 162\: gm \end{matrix}$$
